correctness.rationale: For each private clique C_v of order r_v>=2, a fort with at least two C_v vertices contains a two-vertex fort; minimality forces exactly that pair. With at most one C_v vertex, outside peripheral vertices force core membership equivalent to a unique peripheral choice, giving an exact lift of a fort of G and preserving minimality. A zero-forcing set intersects every fort, proved by the first-force/stalled-white argument. At v not in the induced base forcing set, exactly one clique vertex and core v are white, weight r_v z^(r_v-1); at v in it, local weight z^r_v(r_v+1+z). Multiply to prove the full nonuniform polynomial, minimum exponent, and multiplicity; r_v=2 boundary included. Independently enumerated 74 labelled graph/corona parameter instances with 1<=n<=3 and r_v in {2,3}: direct forts, minimal subset check, greedy forcing sets, and complete coefficients all agree. This finite enumeration corroborates, does not prove, the all-graph theorem.
